RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-503C0E1587-87184
Notice Date: 2026-08-20
Patient: Cameron Foster
Requested Service: Total hip arthroplasty, CPT 27130
Treating Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Aetna Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total hip arthroplasty (CPT 27130), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-20. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that Aetna reverse this determination based on the clinical documentation summarized and enclosed below.

I understand Aetna's medical necessity criteria for hip arthroplasty are set out in Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0287, "Hip Arthroplasty." Below I address each relevant criterion, quoting the plan's own language, and map it to the specific records from my prior authorization packet.

1. Advanced joint disease

The policy states that medical necessity requires:

"Member has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs) from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the hip joint; and Limited range of motion (ROM), antalgic gait, and pain in hip joint with passive ROM on physical examination: and Radiographic evidence of either ... Moderate/severe osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis of the hip joint (Tonnis grade 2 or 3; see Appendix for Tonnis grading scale)."

My records document all of these elements:
- 18 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest, that has become disabling — I ambulate only with a cane, am limited to one block of walking, and cannot put on my own shoes.
- Exam findings of positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated 2026-06-13 showing joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes — findings of advanced osteoarthritis. [Tonnis grade as assessed by the radiologist/Dr. Reyes is not stated in the records provided to me and should be confirmed from the radiology report or Dr. Reyes's operative note.]

2. History of unsuccessful conservative therapy

The policy states:

"History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year."

And further specifies the required components:

"Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (at least 24 weeks for persons with a relative contraindication), including all of the following, unless contraindicated: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy; ADLs diminished despite completing a plan of care). Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history; and Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications ... to joint replacement, optional for others); and Therapeutic injections into the hip (required for persons with relative contraindications ... to joint replacement, optional for others)."

My records satisfy every listed component:
- Supervised, in-person physical therapy: 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 2026-03-24 through 2026-06-30, totaling 24 visits, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the 12-week minimum and is confirmed by the treating physical therapist's own discharge note, satisfying the requirement that PT be confirmed "either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."
- Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics: NSAIDs used for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises: addressed directly through the hip abductor strengthening component of the physical therapy program.
- Activity modification: [records documenting specific activity-modification instructions given to the patient are not included in the summary provided and should be obtained from the treating surgeon's or physical therapist's chart notes, if available.]
- Assistive device use: documented ongoing cane use, with ambulation limited to one block.
- Therapeutic injections into the hip: corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-05, which gave only two weeks of partial relief.

Given that BMI is 29 (not greater than 40) [and age is not stated in the records provided to me], my case does not appear to meet the policy's definition of a "relative contraindication," which the policy defines as:

"Relative contraindications to joint replacement include the following: morbid obesity (body mass index (BMI) greater than 40), age less than 50 years). Persons with relative contraindications should exhaust all non-surgical treatment options."

Accordingly, the applicable conservative-therapy benchmark is the standard 12-week track, not the extended 24-week track, and the enclosed records exceed that requirement.

3. No disqualifying findings

The clinical summary confirms no active infection and no untreated substance use, and there is no evidence in the record of any of the absolute contraindications to hip arthroplasty listed in CPB 0287.

Conclusion

Based on the enclosed records — the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, imaging report, and examination notes — my case documents (a) advanced joint disease with pain, functional disability, and radiographic changes, and (b) a completed course of conservative therapy encompassing supervised physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, assistive device use, and a therapeutic corticosteroid injection, without adequate relief. I therefore ask that Aetna reverse the denial of CPT 27130 and authorize the requested total hip arthroplasty.

Enclosed with this appeal:
1. Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-24 to 2026-06-30, 24 visits)
2. Medication history documenting 4 months of NSAID use
3. Procedure note for corticosteroid injection, 2026-05-05
4. Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and radiology report, 2026-06-13
5. Physical examination notes documenting provocative testing and functional limitations
6. [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes, if not already on file]
7. [Any additional records documenting activity modification, if available]

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-16). Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of any additional information needed. I can be reached at [patient phone number] or [patient email address].

Sincerely,

Cameron Foster
Member ID: W291434326
